title: Fun at Class Party!: Division, Sharing and Grouping
seo_title: Division, Sharing and Grouping Class 3 Worksheet with Answers (Maths Mela Chapter 10)
standard_code: Class 3, Maths Mela Chapter 10: Fun at Class Party!
standard_text: Division as equal sharing and grouping, its relation to multiplication, and solving problems (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 3)
meta_desc: Class 3 Fun at Class Party! worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 10): sharing, grouping, division facts and stories. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Division shares equally or makes equal groups.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Sharing: 20 sweets among 4 children → 20 ÷ 4 = 5 each.
  • Grouping: 20 sweets in packets of 4 → 5 packets.
  • Use a times table: 4 × 5 = 20, so 20 ÷ 4 = 5.

Examples

Example

Share 18 laddoos among 3 friends.

3 × 6 = 18

Answer: 6 each

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Subtracting instead of dividingShare into equal groups.
Using the wrong tableThink: ? × 3 = 18.

faq.q: How are multiplication and division linked?

faq.a: What is left over when things cannot be shared equally.

items.q: Share these 12 counters equally on 3 plates. How many go on each plate?
items.e: Sharing: give the counters out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 3 plates gets 4. 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
Sharing: give the counters out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 4 plates gets 5. 20 ÷ 4 = 5.

items.q: Share these 15 counters equally on 5 plates. How many go on each plate?
items.e: Sharing: give the counters out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 5 plates gets 3. 15 ÷ 5 = 3.
Sharing: give the counters out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 2 plates gets 9. 18 ÷ 2 = 9.
Sharing: give the counters out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 6 plates gets 4. 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

items.q: 20 counters are put in groups of 5. How many groups are there?
items.e: Grouping: you know there are 5 in each group. Count the rings: 4 groups. So 20 ÷ 5 = 4.

items.q: 24 counters are put in groups of 4. How many groups are there?
items.e: Grouping: you know there are 4 in each group. Count the rings: 6 groups. So 24 ÷ 4 = 6.

items.q: 18 counters are put in groups of 3. How many groups are there?
items.e: Grouping: you know there are 3 in each group. Count the rings: 6 groups. So 18 ÷ 3 = 6.
Grouping: you know there are 10 in each group. Count the rings: 3 groups. So 30 ÷ 10 = 3.
28 counters are shared on 4 plates. Each plate has 7. That is 28 ÷ 4 = 7. Always start with the total, 28. 4 ÷ 28 is the wrong way around.
21 counters are shared on 3 plates. Each plate has 7. That is 21 ÷ 3 = 7. Always start with the total, 21. 3 ÷ 21 is the wrong way around.

items.q: 16 counters are shared equally on 2 plates. Which division matches the picture?
items.e: 16 counters are shared on 2 plates. Each plate has 8. That is 16 ÷ 2 = 8. Always start with the total, 16. 2 ÷ 16 is the wrong way around.

items.q: Which one is grouping?
items.e: Grouping means you know how many go in each group. “Bags of 5” tells you there are 5 in each bag. 20 ÷ 5 = 4 bags. Sharing among 5 bags is sharing: you know the number of bags.

items.q: Which one is sharing?
c: Put 18 hockey cards in piles of 3.
items.e: Sharing means you know how many groups. “Among 3 friends” tells you there are 3 groups. 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cards each. Piles of 3 is grouping: you know how many go in each pile.

items.q: What is 42 ÷ 6? Think: 6 × ☐ = 42.
items.e: Think multiplication: 6 × ☐ = 42. 6 × 7 = 42, so 42 ÷ 6 = 7.

items.q: What is 56 ÷ 8? Think: 8 × ☐ = 56.
items.e: Think multiplication: 8 × ☐ = 56. 8 × 7 = 56, so 56 ÷ 8 = 7.
You can multiply in any order and get the same answer. 2 × 9 = 18, so 9 × 2 = 18 too.
You can multiply in any order and get the same answer. 5 × 8 = 40, so 8 × 5 = 40 too.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 9 × 5?
items.e: 5 × 9 is 9 × 5 turned around. Both make 45.

items.q: Share these 12 counters equally between 3 plates. How many go on each plate?
items.e: Sharing: give the counters out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each of the 3 plates gets 4. 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
Sharing: give the counters out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each of the 4 plates gets 5. 20 ÷ 4 = 5.

items.q: Share these 15 counters equally between 5 bags. How many go in each bag?
items.e: Sharing: give the counters out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each of the 5 bags gets 3. 15 ÷ 5 = 3.
Sharing: give the counters out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each of the 2 boxes gets 9. 18 ÷ 2 = 9.

items.q: 20 counters are put into groups of 5. How many groups are there?
items.e: Grouping: you know there are 5 in each group. Count the rings: 4 groups. So 20 ÷ 5 = 4.

items.q: 24 counters are put into groups of 4. How many groups are there?
items.e: Grouping: you know there are 4 in each group. Count the rings: 6 groups. So 24 ÷ 4 = 6.
24 counters are shared between 4 plates. Each plate has 6. That is 24 ÷ 4 = 6.

items.q: 15 counters are shared equally between 3 plates. Which division does the picture show?
items.e: 15 counters are shared between 3 plates. Each plate has 5. That is 15 ÷ 3 = 5.

items.q: What is 80 ÷ 4? Think: 8 ÷ 4 = 2.
items.e: 80 is 8 tens. 8 tens ÷ 4 = 2 tens = 20. Not 2: the answer is tens, not ones.

items.q: What is 60 ÷ 3? Think: 6 ÷ 3 = 2.
items.e: 60 is 6 tens. 6 tens ÷ 3 = 2 tens = 20. Not 2: the answer is tens, not ones.

items.q: What is 40 ÷ 2? Think: 4 ÷ 2 = 2.
items.e: 40 is 4 tens. 4 tens ÷ 2 = 2 tens = 20. Not 2: the answer is tens, not ones.

items.q: What is 50 ÷ 5? Think: 5 ÷ 5 = 1.
items.e: 50 is 5 tens. 5 tens ÷ 5 = 1 ten = 10. Not 1: the answer is tens, not ones.

items.q: 48 is partitioned like this. What is 48 ÷ 4?
69 is partitioned like this. What is 69 ÷ 3?
What is 84 ÷ 4?
72 is partitioned like this. What is 72 ÷ 3?
items.e: 7 tens do not share equally into 3, so use 72 = 60 + 12. 60 ÷ 3 = 20 and 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Add: 20 + 4 = 24. Check: 24 × 3 = 72.
Ask: 2 times what makes 16? 16 ÷ 2 = 8. Check: 2 × 8 = 16, so ? = 8.
Ask: 5 times what makes 45? 45 ÷ 5 = 9. Check: 5 × 9 = 45, so ? = 9.
Ask: 10 times what makes 40? 40 ÷ 10 = 4. Check: 10 × 4 = 40, so ? = 4.
Ask: 5 times what makes 15? 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Check: 5 × 3 = 15, so ? = 3.
Think: 2 × ? = 14. 2 × 7 = 14, so 14 ÷ 2 = 7. The answer is not 14: that is the number you started with.
Think: 5 × ? = 20. 5 × 4 = 20, so 20 ÷ 5 = 4. The answer is not 20: that is the number you started with.
Think: 10 × ? = 60. 10 × 6 = 60, so 60 ÷ 10 = 6. The answer is not 60: that is the number you started with.
Think: 2 × ? = 18. 2 × 9 = 18, so 18 ÷ 2 = 9. The answer is not 18: that is the number you started with.
Think: 5 × ? = 40. 5 × 8 = 40, so 40 ÷ 5 = 8. The answer is not 40: that is the number you started with.
Think: 10 × ? = 90. 10 × 9 = 90, so 90 ÷ 10 = 9. The answer is not 90: that is the number you started with.
Think: 2 × ? = 12. 2 × 6 = 12, so 12 ÷ 2 = 6. The answer is not 12: that is the number you started with.
Think: 5 × ? = 35. 5 × 7 = 35, so 35 ÷ 5 = 7. The answer is not 35: that is the number you started with.

items.q: 12 counters are put into groups of 2. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the groups: there are 6 groups of 2. 12 ÷ 2 = 6. Check: 6 × 2 = 12.

items.q: 30 counters are put into groups of 10. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the groups: there are 3 groups of 10. 30 ÷ 10 = 3. Check: 3 × 10 = 30.
Ask: 3 times what makes 18? 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Check: 3 × 6 = 18, so ? = 6.
Ask: 8 times what makes 56? 56 ÷ 8 = 7. Check: 8 × 7 = 56, so ? = 7.

items.q: Which division fact goes with 6 × 7 = 42?
items.e: Division undoes multiplication. 6 groups of 7 make 42, so 42 split into groups of 7 makes 6 groups: 42 ÷ 7 = 6. Start with the biggest number, 42.

items.q: Which division fact goes with 4 × 9 = 36?
items.e: Division undoes multiplication. 4 groups of 9 make 36, so 36 split into groups of 9 makes 4 groups: 36 ÷ 9 = 4. Start with the biggest number, 36.

items.q: Which division fact goes with 8 × 5 = 40?
items.e: Division undoes multiplication. 8 groups of 5 make 40, so 40 split into groups of 5 makes 8 groups: 40 ÷ 5 = 8. Start with the biggest number, 40.

items.q: Which division fact goes with 7 × 8 = 56?
items.e: Division undoes multiplication. 7 groups of 8 make 56, so 56 split into groups of 8 makes 7 groups: 56 ÷ 8 = 7. Start with the biggest number, 56.

items.q: Which division fact goes with 9 × 6 = 54?
items.e: Division undoes multiplication. 9 groups of 6 make 54, so 54 split into groups of 6 makes 9 groups: 54 ÷ 6 = 9. Start with the biggest number, 54.

items.q: Which is not in the fact family for 3, 8 and 24?
items.e: The fact family is 3 × 8 = 24, 8 × 3 = 24, 24 ÷ 3 = 8 and 24 ÷ 8 = 3. 3 ÷ 24 = 8 is wrong: in these facts the biggest number, 24, comes first when you divide.

items.q: Which is not in the fact family for 5, 6 and 30?
items.e: The fact family is 5 × 6 = 30, 6 × 5 = 30, 30 ÷ 5 = 6 and 30 ÷ 6 = 5. 5 ÷ 30 = 6 is wrong: in these facts the biggest number, 30, comes first when you divide.

items.q: Which is not in the fact family for 4, 7 and 28?
items.e: The fact family is 4 × 7 = 28, 7 × 4 = 28, 28 ÷ 4 = 7 and 28 ÷ 7 = 4. 4 ÷ 28 = 7 is wrong: in these facts the biggest number, 28, comes first when you divide.

items.q: Which is not in the fact family for 9, 10 and 90?
items.e: The fact family is 9 × 10 = 90, 10 × 9 = 90, 90 ÷ 9 = 10 and 90 ÷ 10 = 9. 9 ÷ 90 = 10 is wrong: in these facts the biggest number, 90, comes first when you divide.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ ÷ 4 = 7
items.e: Use multiplication to undo the division: ☐ = 7 × 4 = 28. Check: 28 ÷ 4 = 7.

items.q: 17 counters are put into groups of 5. What is 17 ÷ 5?
items.e: 3 × 5 = 15 and 4 × 5 = 20, which is too many. So 3 groups of 5, and 17 − 15 = 2 left over. The remainder is always less than 5.
5 × 4 = 20 and 6 × 4 = 24, which is too many. So 5 groups of 4, and 23 − 20 = 3 left over. The remainder is always less than 4.

items.q: What is 14 ÷ 3?
items.e: 4 × 3 = 12 and 5 × 3 = 15, which is too many. So 4 groups of 3, and 14 − 12 = 2 left over. The remainder is always less than 3.

items.q: What is 22 ÷ 5?
items.e: 4 × 5 = 20 and 5 × 5 = 25, which is too many. So 4 groups of 5, and 22 − 20 = 2 left over. The remainder is always less than 5.

items.q: What is 19 ÷ 2?
items.e: 9 × 2 = 18 and 10 × 2 = 20, which is too many. So 9 groups of 2, and 19 − 18 = 1 left over. The remainder is always less than 2.

items.q: 26 students have lunch at tables. 4 students sit at each table. How many tables are needed so every student has a seat?
items.e: 26 ÷ 4 = 6 r 2. 6 tables seat 24 students. The 2 students left over need one more table, so 7 tables.

items.q: Rehan puts 29 cards into 3 equal piles. How many cards are left over?
items.e: 9 × 3 = 27 and 10 × 3 = 30, which is too many. So each pile has 9 cards, and 29 − 27 = 2 are left over.

items.q: There are 4 rows of chairs. Each row has 6 chairs. How many chairs are there? Which number sentence matches the story?
items.e: 4 equal rows of 6 is multiplication: 4 × 6 = ☐. 6 + 6 + 6 only counts 3 rows.

items.q: Gauri shares 24 stickers equally among 4 friends. How many stickers does each friend get? Which number sentence matches the story?
items.e: Sharing equally is division: 24 ÷ 4 = ☐. Each friend gets 6.

items.q: Nikhil puts 35 cards in piles of 5. How many piles does he make? Which number sentence matches the story?
items.e: Making groups of 5 is division (grouping): 35 ÷ 5 = ☐. Start with the total, 35. He makes 7 piles.

items.q: There are 4 rows of chairs at assembly. Each row has 23 chairs. How many chairs are there?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 23 × 4. Partition 23 = 20 + 3. 20 × 4 = 80 and 3 × 4 = 12. Add: 80 + 12 = 92. The answer is 92 chairs.

items.q: A relay team at the swimming carnival has 4 swimmers. There are 16 teams. How many swimmers is that?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 16 × 4. Partition 16 = 10 + 6. 10 × 4 = 40 and 6 × 4 = 24. Add: 40 + 24 = 64. The answer is 64 swimmers.

items.q: Two buses take Class 3 on a school excursion. Each bus has 45 seats. How many seats is that altogether?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 45 × 2. Partition 45 = 40 + 5. 40 × 2 = 80 and 5 × 2 = 10. Add: 80 + 10 = 90. The answer is 90 seats.

items.q: A packet has 12 sausages. The school buys 5 packets for the sausage sizzle. How many sausages is that?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 12 × 5. Partition 12 = 10 + 2. 10 × 5 = 50 and 2 × 5 = 10. Add: 50 + 10 = 60. The answer is 60 sausages.

items.q: An AFL team has 18 players on the field. How many players are on the field when 2 teams play?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 18 × 2. Partition 18 = 10 + 8. 10 × 2 = 20 and 8 × 2 = 16. Add: 20 + 16 = 36. The answer is 36 players.

items.q: A cricket team has 11 players. 4 teams play at a school cricket day. How many players is that?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 11 × 4. Partition 11 = 10 + 1. 10 × 4 = 40 and 1 × 4 = 4. Add: 40 + 4 = 44. The answer is 44 players.

items.q: Priya shares ₹24 equally between 3 children. How much does each child get?
items.e: Sharing equally: ₹24 ÷ 3. 3 × 8 = 24, so each child gets ₹8.

items.q: The school chooks laid 30 eggs. The eggs are packed in boxes of 6. How many boxes are filled?
items.e: Grouping in 6s: 30 ÷ 6. 5 × 6 = 30, so 5 boxes are filled.

items.q: 96 students are split equally into 4 sport houses. How many students are in each house?
64 chairs are set out in 4 equal rows for assembly. How many chairs are in each row?
A tricycle has 3 wheels. Rahul sees 6 tricycles in the playground. How many wheels is that?
items.e: 6 tricycles with 3 wheels each: 6 × 3 = 18. 9 is 6 + 3, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: A spider has 8 legs. Rohan finds 5 spiders in the garden. How many legs is that altogether?
items.e: 5 × 8 = 40. 32 is only 4 spiders.

items.q: Yoghurts come in packs of 4. Kavya buys 7 packs. How many yoghurts is that?
items.e: 7 packs of 4: 7 × 4 = 28. Double 7 is 14, double 14 is 28.

items.q: In a classroom, 3 children sit at each table. There are 9 tables. How many children are there?
items.e: 9 tables of 3: 9 × 3 = 27. 24 is only 8 tables.

items.q: A car has 4 wheels. There are 8 cars in the car park. How many wheels is that?
items.e: 8 × 4 = 32. Double 8 is 16, double 16 is 32.

items.q: An octopus has 8 arms. There are 3 octopuses at the aquarium. How many arms is that?
items.e: 3 × 8 = 24. 11 is 3 + 8, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: A chair has 4 legs. How many legs do 9 chairs have?
items.e: 9 × 4 = 36. Double 9 is 18, double 18 is 36.

items.q: A football team gets 3 points for a win. The team wins 7 games. How many points is that?
items.e: 7 wins with 3 points each: 7 × 3 = 21.

items.q: Pencils come in packs of 8. Isha’s teacher buys 6 packs. How many pencils is that?
There are 21 wheels on some tricycles. How many tricycles are there?
items.e: Each tricycle has 3 wheels. 21 ÷ 3 = ? 3 × 7 = 21, so there are 7 tricycles.
